Photo 2 shows the same laptop from a side angle, revealing ports on the left side (USB, HDMI, etc.) and the textured palm rest. The screen displays the same wallpaper.

Dell logo visible on the bezel below the screen in photo 1 and photo 2.
Intel Core i7 sticker visible on the lower right of the palm rest in photo 1 and photo 2.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the bottom chassis or hinge area showing the model label (e.g., 'XPS 15 9570') or a screenshot of the System Information window showing the exact model name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic Dell laptop with i7 and GTX 1050, not as the premium XPS 15 9570.

risks.risk: The processor may not be 8th gen, possibly 7th gen or lower, affecting performance and value.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the System Information window showing the CPU name (e.g., Intel Core i7-8750H) or the Device Manager/Properties window with CPU details.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a laptop with unspecified i7 generation, which may be lower than 8th gen.

risks.risk: The laptop may have physical damage or wear not visible in the photos, such as screen dead pixels, keyboard issues, or hinge problems.
risks.proof: A close-up video or photo of the screen under different lighting, keyboard keys, and hinge movement.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming minor wear, but with a discount for potential unseen damage.

risks.risk: The laptop may not be in working condition or may have software issues (e.g., Windows activation, drivers).
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop booting up, running a benchmark, and accessing system settings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, since 'works' is unproven.

A screenshot of the System Information window showing the CPU name and model.
A video showing the laptop booting up and running a simple task (e.g., opening a browser).
A close-up photo of the screen under different lighting to check for dead pixels.
